text.p: Here is how major stock markets outside the United States ended on Wednesday.

LONDON - Shares ended lower as the antics of the volatile Dow scared investors away and another call for higher interest rates by the Bank of England sent gilts scurrying lower. The FTSE 100 share index ended 29.9 points lower at 4,207.5.

FRANKFURT - Overnight volatility on Wall Street and a see-sawing response to key U.S. economic data in the afternoon unsettled the share market, and prices finally ended the day at lower levels. The IBIS DAX index, which tracks all-day screen dealings in German blue chips, closed the day at 2,997.95. Earlier, the DAX index, which was catching up on a surge in late screen trading Tuesday, ended floor trade at 2,999.20, 9.87 points higher than Tuesday's mid-afternoon close.

PARIS - Shares finished a nervous session in loss but off the lows as a rising Dow rode to the rescue in the afternoon. Traders said Paris dipped to a loss of 1.5 percent as the markets whipsawed after a U.S. durable goods report showed a 1.7 percent fall instead of an expected increase. The blue-chip CAC-40 index closed down 17.75 points at 2,465.01.

ZURICH - A stronger opening on Wall Street led to a recovery of Swiss shares in late trade, but Swiss indices still ended weaker after Tuesday's record close. Dealers said worries about a possible U.S. interest rate hike may keep a lid on the market ahead of the U.S. FOMC meeting on February 4-5. The all-share SPI fell 10.04 points to 2,666.63 points.

TOKYO - Stocks rose sharply, as the yen's fall to a fresh 47-month low against the dollar fuelled buying of shares in multinational companies. The market's key barometer, the Nikkei average of 225 leading shares, jumped by 538.73 points or 3.03 percent to close at 18,335.30.

HONG KONG - Stocks ended with heavy losses, beaten down by interest rate concerns and a slide in the property sector after recommendations that banks curb lending for luxury property acquisitions. The Hang Seng Index fell 117.86 points to 13,285.43. Turnover was HK$11.89 billion versus Tuesday's HK$8.64 billion.

SYDNEY - The share market kept a firm grip on its gains to close higher with options-related trade ahead of Thursday's January expiry and well-received inflation data underpinning the rise. The All Ordinaries index added 10.0 points to 2,414.2.

JOHANNESBURG - Gold shares took a battering as the bullion price lost all Tuesday's gains and fell to $351 an ounce, threatening to test the key $350 an ounce level. Having climbed nearly five percent on Tuesday, riding the brief rally in the gold price, gold shares shed more than three percent. The gold index lost 43.8 points to 1,385.3 points. Industrial shares also took a bashing, with the index shedding 48.5 points to 6,687.5. Weakness in golds and industrials combined to knock the all-share index 48.5 points down to 6,687.5.
